name: Secondary Erythromelalgia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical features and exclusion

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of burning pain primarily affecting extremities
Erythema and increased skin temperature in affected areas during episodes
Presence of an underlying systemic condition known to cause secondary erythromelalgia (e.g., myeloproliferative disorders, autoimmune diseases)
Symptom relief upon cooling of affected areas
Exclusion of primary (genetic) erythromelalgia by history and genetic testing if indicated

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of episodic burning pain with erythema and warmth in extremities plus identification of an underlying causative disorder
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and requires exclusion of primary erythromelalgia and other mimics.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Episodic burning pain of distal extremities
pathognomonic.notes: Typically triggered by heat or exertion
searchTerms: burning pain in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Erythema localized to hands and feet during attacks
searchTerms: redness on hands and feet during attacks

pathognomonic.symptomName: Increased skin temperature in affected areas during episodes

common.symptomName: Symptom relief with cooling or cold exposure
Swelling of affected extremities during attacks
searchTerms: swelling in hands and feet during attacks

common.symptomName: Hyperesthesia or allodynia in affected areas

occasional.symptomName: Ulceration or skin breakdown in chronic cases
Fatigue related to underlying systemic disease

searchTerms: sensitivity to cold after symptoms improve

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness or discomfort in affected limbs

rare.symptomName: Digital gangrene in severe untreated cases
Systemic symptoms related to underlying disorder (e.g., weight loss, fever)

laboratory: Elevated platelet count or hematocrit in myeloproliferative disorders
Normal inflammatory markers in isolated erythromelalgia
imaging: Doppler ultrasound may show normal or increased blood flow in affected limbs
Nerve conduction studies may reveal peripheral neuropathy
genetic: Absence of SCN9A mutations typical for primary erythromelalgia
other: Symptom provocation by heat exposure and relief by cooling
Skin biopsy may show nonspecific vascular changes

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset, often in childhood or adolescence
History of trauma or surgery preceding symptoms
Presence of trophic skin changes and motor dysfunction
Different pattern of pain distribution and autonomic features
Absence of episodic erythema and warmth

redFlags: Rapid progression to digital ulceration or gangrene
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
Underlying hematological malignancy or myeloproliferative disorder
references: Mork C, et al. Secondary erythromelalgia: clinical features and treatment. J Clin Rheumatol. 2020.
Davis MD, et al. Erythromelalgia: vasculopathy, neuropathy, or both? Arch Dermatol. 2000.
